Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Older adults with low serum 25OHD levels were more likely to have elevated depressive symptoms overall.
Sentence: "Overall, there was a significant association between low 25OHD levels and elevated depressive symptoms (odds ratio [OR] = 1.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.20-2.07 for the lowest quartile; OR = 1.45, 95% CI = 1.15-1.83 for <30 nmol/L cut-off and OR = 1.34, 95% CI = 1.10-1.62 for the ≤50 nmol/L cut-off) after adjustment for a wide range of covariates of clinical significance."
Measured as: elevated depressive symptoms (CES-D)
Population: Older adults from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level (observational, no intervention)
Comparator: Higher 25OHD levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 5,607
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: 25OHD levels did not differ significantly between patients treated for depression and healthy controls.
Sentence: "The level of 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D3 did not differ significantly between the examined groups."
Measured as: depression (patients treated for depression vs healthy controls)
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression and 45 healthy subjects
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
